subject: Chemistry
question: A 2.00 dm³ sample of nitrogen at −20 °C and 100 kPa is warmed to 30 °C at constant pressure. Calculate its new volume.
response_text:
Temperatures must be in kelvin:
T₁ = −20 °C = 293 K
T₂ = 30 °C = 303 K

At constant pressure V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂, so
V₂ = V₁ × T₂/T₁ = 2.00 × 303/293 = 2.07 dm³

faults.note: stem-cnv (explicit °C to K conversion, affine offset applied): −20 °C = 253.15 K; stated 293 K (the sign of −20 was lost); tau = 0, h = 0.5. True V₂ = 2.00 × 303.15/253.15 = 2.40 dm³; the final arithmetic holds as written but carries the slip. [computed: exact=253.15 stated=293 (in SI) h=0.5 -> does not hold]
